Rust compiles to WebAssembly: near-native speed in the browser, a small binary, and the same language on both sides of the wire.

When it is worth it

Use WASM Do not use WASM
CPU-heavy work: parsing, codecs, crypto, simulation ordinary UI and forms
Reusing an existing Rust library in the browser anything the DOM does well
Image/video/audio processing a page that is mostly text
Games and graphics CRUD apps
Running untrusted code in a sandbox when bundle size dominates

WASM's real win is sharing logic: the same validation, parser or pricing engine running on the server and in the browser, with no reimplementation and no drift.

crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"] matters: cdylib for the wasm artifact, rlib so you can still unit-test the crate natively with cargo test.

Working with JS values

Gotcha: passing complex data across the boundary costs. Every JsValue conversion copies. For hot paths, keep the data on the Rust side and pass handles (integers) instead of structures.

A real app: the Yew framework

Framework Model Notes
leptos fine-grained signals fastest, closest to SolidJS
yew React-like components mature, familiar
dioxus React-like, multi-target also desktop/mobile/TUI
sycamore signals smaller community

Trunk: the build tool

Trunk compiles the Rust, runs wasm-bindgen, runs wasm-opt, hashes assets and serves with hot reload. It removes the whole npm layer for a pure-Rust frontend.

Size and speed

Setting Rough effect
opt-level = "s" −10–20% size vs 3
lto = true −10%
panic = "abort" −10–15%
wasm-opt -Oz −10–20%
No std formatting −30% (big)

format! and Display pull in a large chunk of std. In a size-sensitive WASM build, avoid them in hot paths — or go no_std.

Enable gzip/brotli on the server: WASM compresses to about 30% of its size, and the browser caches it.

Threads and SIMD (advanced)

SIMD is widely supported. Threads require SharedArrayBuffer, which needs cross-origin isolation headers:

Without those two headers, SharedArrayBuffer is undefined and any thread-based WASM fails.

WASM outside the browser

The same .wasm runs in:

  • Cloudflare Workers / Fastly Compute — edge functions.
  • WASI (wasm32-wasip1) — server-side sandboxing, plugins.
  • Extism — a plugin system for any host language.
  • Wasmtime — an embeddable runtime.

A plugin architecture where untrusted customer code runs in a WASM sandbox with explicit host functions is one of the genuinely great uses of this technology.

Exercises

  1. Build the slugify module with wasm-pack and call it from a plain HTML page.
  2. Add console_error_panic_hook and trigger a panic; read the message in the console.
  3. Pass a Vec<Order> from JS to Rust as JsValue and return the total.
  4. Build a Yew counter, then a Leptos counter, and compare bundle sizes.
  5. Take a WASM build and shrink it with opt-level = "s", lto, panic = "abort" and wasm-opt -Oz. Report each step's size.
  6. Explain why crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"] is needed to keep cargo test working.
